Done-when: 'Add tools/build_single_file.py after the package split. Done when: the generated file passes the same aggregate self-test as the package.' tools/build_single_file.py added: generate_source() locates the facade's pathminer.core bootstrap by sentinel comments and replaces it with pathminer/core/geometry.py and pathminer/core/solver.py inlined into throwaway module objects, so the generated file has no import-time dependency on pathminer at all (test_generated_single_file_has_no_pathminer_package_dependency; also manually verified by running the generated file from /tmp with a minimal env). --check regenerates the file and diffs its --selftest vector-by-vector against the split facade's: 118/118 both headless; 284/284 both with --board against the real IP5385 board. Coordinator review found and this session fixed check() TWICE: round 1, a false PASS when both sides' --selftest failed identically (e.g. both '0/1 checks passed', exit 1) because check() only compared the two runs against each other and never confirmed either had actually passed; round 2, a false PASS on internally inconsistent output - exit 0 and a summary claiming a full pass (e.g. '118/118 checks passed') while the actually-printed vector lines don't add up to that (e.g. one printed [PASS] line) - because round 1 never cross-checked parsed vector/PASS counts against the summary. check() now requires, per side, independently: exit 0, a parseable summary, passed==total, no FAIL vector, parsed vector count == summary total, and parsed PASS count == summary passed. Four regression tests across both rounds pin these (three from round 1, one new in round 2). This evidence entry reflects the twice-corrected, no-longer-falsifiable check().

decisions: Aliases (name = _pm_solver.name / _pm_geometry.name), not wrappers, wherever the v0.13 signature already matched the pathminer.core one exactly, so is-identity can be asserted directly as proof of one shared dispatcher rather than trusting a numeric coincidence.

network_resistance keeps its own r<=0 pre-filter and explicit dense/sparse crossover computed from len(adj) vs dense_limit (the same test this function has always used), then delegates only the actual linear solve to pathminer.core.solver.two_terminal_resistance with an explicit backend= override - not left to that function's own 'auto', which counts nodes from the post-filter edge list and could pick a different crossover point on a graph with dropped edges.

The pathminer.core bootstrap in tools/pcb_trace_resistance.py is delimited by explicit sentinel comments (PATHMINER_CORE_BOOTSTRAP_BEGIN/END), not AST slicing or a fixed line range, so tools/build_single_file.py can find and replace exactly the right block regardless of unrelated edits elsewhere, and fails loudly (RuntimeError) if the sentinels are ever missing or renamed.

Inlined pathminer.core modules become throwaway types.ModuleType objects bound to the existing _pm_geometry/_pm_solver names (not `from x import *`), so every downstream call site in the facade works unchanged in the generated single file.

tools/build_single_file.py --check compares parsed [PASS]/[FAIL] <name> identity and totals, not raw got/want text, because a few vectors (V19, V23) legitimately print a fresh tempfile.mkdtemp() path on every run - the same reason tests/baseline/regression_compare.py normalizes those fields before comparing against a frozen golden fixture.

network_resistance's stricter failure behavior on invalid input (a named ValueError for a disconnected/invalid network, inherited from pathminer.core.solver's already-reviewed _prepare validation) was accepted, not defended against, after the full regression run showed it unchanged before/after and a new failure-path test (test_network_resistance_raises_on_a_disconnected_graph) confirmed the new behavior; no acceptance vector or real-board path exercises the previously inconsistent behavior with a valid answer.
